title: Arrays and Strings
description: This module dives deep into the concepts of arrays and strings—two of the most fundamental data structures in computer science. You'll learn how data is stored in memory, how to access and manipulate it efficiently, and how to solve common problems involving arrays and strings. The module also emphasizes time and space complexity analysis, pattern recognition, and practical code examples to build your problem-solving confidence.

lessons.title: Understanding Arrays
lessons.content: Arrays are a collection of elements stored at contiguous memory locations. They allow random access using indices and are used to store multiple items of the same type together. Understanding how memory is allocated for arrays is key to understanding performance trade-offs.

lessons.title: Basic Operations on Arrays
Common Array Problems and Techniques
lessons.content:
Learn to solve problems like:
- Finding the maximum/minimum element
- Reversing an array
- Rotating an array
- Removing duplicates

These problems improve your understanding of indexing, loops, and memory efficiency.

lessons.title: Two Pointer Technique
Sliding Window Technique
What are Strings in Programming?
lessons.content: Strings are sequences of characters, usually implemented as arrays of characters terminated by a null character (`\0`) in low-level languages like C or as objects in high-level languages like JavaScript and Python. Strings are essential in representing textual data and are widely used in pattern searching, parsing, and user input.

lessons.title: String Operations and Methods
Reversing a String
String Pattern Matching: Naive vs. KMP
lessons.content: Pattern matching algorithms are used to find substrings within a main string. The naive approach compares the pattern with each substring one-by-one, which has O(m*n) complexity. Knuth-Morris-Pratt (KMP) improves this by preprocessing the pattern to skip unnecessary comparisons, achieving O(n + m) complexity.

Multidimensional Arrays
Common String Interview Problems
lessons.content:
Understand and practice problems like:
- Palindrome check
- Longest common prefix
- Longest substring without repeating characters
- Count and say

These strengthen your logic, understanding of character-level manipulations, and usage of hash maps or sets.
